description: Deployment surface for the image queue: systemd env examples and the web unit updated so the player and web server share ONE queue directory, the web unit granted write access to it (ReadWritePaths) with ffmpeg noted as a new web runtime dependency, and DEPLOY-WEB.md extended with the upload page, the shared queue dir, the write-access requirement, the ffmpeg dependency, the size cap, and a 'run the webapp locally and upload from your phone' section. Depends on FEAT-001 and FEAT-002 because it documents the exact config names (VSMP_QUEUE, --queue-dir, VSMP_ARCHIVE_DIR/VSMP_ARCHIVE_MAX) and behaviour those features introduced. No code; verified by the full suite staying green plus a config/docs review.
steps: systemd/vsmp-web.env.example: add VSMP_QUEUE=/path/to/queue with a comment that it MUST be the same directory the player's --queue-dir / VSMP_QUEUE points at. If FEAT-001/FEAT-002 exposed the archive knobs, document VSMP_ARCHIVE_DIR and VSMP_ARCHIVE_MAX here too (commented out, off by default).

systemd/vsmp.env.example: document that the player uses the same queue directory — either by adding --queue-dir=/path/to/queue to the VSMP_ARGS guidance or by noting VSMP_QUEUE must match the web unit's value. Make the 'same directory' requirement explicit and hard to miss.

systemd/vsmp-web.service: the web unit now needs WRITE access to the queue dir. Replace the current ReadOnlyPaths line with the repo kept readable plus ReadWritePaths=<queue dir> (point the example at a concrete path consistent with the env example, and keep a comment explaining it must match VSMP_QUEUE). Add a prominent note that ffmpeg is now a RUNTIME dependency of the web service (not only the player), since POST /upload shells out to it for conversion. Keep the other hardening directives intact.

DEPLOY-WEB.md: add the /upload route to the 'What it serves' table; add a section describing the shared queue directory and that the web service must have write access to it (cross-reference the ReadWritePaths change); note ffmpeg is required by the web service now; document the 16MB upload size cap (MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH) and the clean 413 behaviour; add a 'Run the webapp locally and upload from your phone' section based on design doc section 7 (python3 webapp.py, open http://<laptop-LAN-ip>:8080/upload from a phone on the same wifi, upload JPEG/PNG/HEIC, confirm a finished 800x480 grayscale PNG appears in queue/, note conversion is real ffmpeg and needs no panel). Keep the existing 'extending it later' write-access note consistent with the now-implemented queue write path.
acceptance_criteria: systemd/vsmp-web.env.example and systemd/vsmp.env.example both reference the queue directory and make explicit it is the SAME directory for player and web server.
systemd/vsmp-web.service grants write access to the queue dir via ReadWritePaths (no longer purely ReadOnlyPaths) and notes ffmpeg as a web runtime dependency.
DEPLOY-WEB.md documents the upload page, the shared queue dir + write-access requirement, the ffmpeg dependency, the 16MB size cap, and includes a local 'upload from your phone' section.
No code regressions: `python3 tests/run.py` stays green with only the optional real-movie checks skipped.
verification: grep -n VSMP_QUEUE systemd/vsmp-web.env.example systemd/vsmp.env.example && grep -n ReadWritePaths systemd/vsmp-web.service && grep -ni ffmpeg systemd/vsmp-web.service DEPLOY-WEB.md
findings:
Docs/systemd only, no code changed. Both FEAT-003 verification commands pass. Full suite green: 252 passed, 0 failed, 4 skipped (the 4 skips are the pre-existing optional VSMP_TEST_MOVIE real-movie checks). Flask/Werkzeug/Pillow are NOT on the system python3 here, so I recreated a throwaway venv at /tmp/vsmp-venv (Flask==3.1.3, Werkzeug==3.1.3, pillow==10.3.0) and ran `/tmp/vsmp-venv/bin/python tests/run.py` -- same approach FEAT-002 documented. Nothing installed into the repo; venv lives outside it.

Config names used (matched to FEAT-001/FEAT-002 implementation): VSMP_QUEUE (the single env var configuring the SAME queue dir for both player and web server), player --queue-dir, VSMP_ARCHIVE_DIR / VSMP_ARCHIVE_MAX (archive knobs, default 50, off unless VSMP_ARCHIVE_DIR set), VSMP_UPLOAD_SECRET (the disabled-by-default upload auth hook), MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH = 16 MB -> clean 413. Example queue path used consistently everywhere: /home/pi/vsmp/queue.

Changes made:
- systemd/vsmp-web.env.example: added VSMP_QUEUE (uncommented, with a comment that it MUST equal the player's --queue-dir / VSMP_QUEUE), plus commented-out VSMP_ARCHIVE_DIR/VSMP_ARCHIVE_MAX (documented as player-read but configured alongside) and VSMP_UPLOAD_SECRET (off by default).
- systemd/vsmp.env.example: added a prominent 'IMAGE QUEUE -- SHARED DIRECTORY' section plus a --queue-dir example line in the VSMP_ARGS guidance, and an uncommented VSMP_QUEUE, all stressing the same-directory requirement and that it must match the web unit's value.
- systemd/vsmp-web.service: added Environment=VSMP_QUEUE=/home/pi/vsmp/queue; added a prominent 'RUNTIME DEPENDENCY: ffmpeg' note (POST /upload shells out to ffmpeg/ffprobe in-request); replaced the purely-ReadOnlyPaths hardening with ReadOnlyPaths=<repo> + ReadWritePaths=/home/pi/vsmp/queue (the one writable path), with comments tying it to VSMP_QUEUE. NOTE: the old ReadOnlyPaths pointed at /home/rpi5/development/vsmp which disagreed with WorkingDirectory (/home/pi/vsmp); I aligned both path lines to /home/pi/vsmp to match WorkingDirectory and the env examples. Other hardening directives (NoNewPrivileges, ProtectSystem=strict, ProtectHome, PrivateTmp) left intact.
- DEPLOY-WEB.md: added /upload and /queue.json rows to the 'What it serves' table; added an ffmpeg-is-now-a-web-dependency note under 'Install the dependencies'; added 4 config-table rows (VSMP_QUEUE, VSMP_ARCHIVE_DIR, VSMP_ARCHIVE_MAX, VSMP_UPLOAD_SECRET); added a 'The shared upload queue' section (shared dir, write-access/ReadWritePaths cross-reference, .incoming/.showing layout, archive behaviour, and the 16MB cap + clean 413 subsection); added a 'Run the webapp locally and upload from your phone' section (python3 webapp.py, open http://<laptop-LAN-ip>:8080/upload from a phone on the same wifi, upload JPEG/PNG/HEIC, verify an 800x480 'L' PNG in queue/, no panel needed, real ffmpeg); and rewrote the 'extending it later' write-access bullet to reference the now-implemented ReadWritePaths queue path.

No user-visible/behaviour change was required beyond the documented path alignment, so no send_message warning was needed.
